sections.h2: Where do I find the Benzie County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Go to Suite 202 of the Government Center, 448 Court Place, Beulah, MI 49617. The counter staffs weekdays from half past eight in the morning to five in the afternoon, and callers reach it at 231-882-0016.

Benzie County hugs Lake Michigan on the northwest side of the state, and its website advertises more than 100 lakes and several square miles of state forest. Every deed, mortgage and easement for land in those townships and in the city of Frankfort lands in the same index at this one counter.

  • Clerks cannot supply blank forms or weigh in on legal questions. People who need a deed written are told to see an attorney or a title company.
  • A filing can arrive over the counter, by post, via UPS or FedEx, or by electronic submission.
  • If you request copies by mail, enclose your own return envelope with postage.

sections.h2: What is the price of recording at the Benzie County office?
sections.html:
The county page quotes $30.00 per filing however many pages it runs. Michigan's MCL 600.2567 sets that same $30 and includes the survey fee inside it. If one paper assigns or discharges multiple instruments, each instrument after the first brings a $3.00 surcharge.

Benzie County recording office charges. Source: Benzie County Register of Deeds page and MCL 600.2567.

Certain papers need a County Treasurer certificate first: warranty deeds, any deed that promises warranty, land contracts and assignments of them, and condominium master deeds. Under MCL 211.135 the proof covers five years of taxes before the instrument date.

sections.h2: Can I record electronically in Benzie County, and is there a surcharge?
sections.html:
Four vendors handle electronic submissions: Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm. Every one sets a price of its own, and the county Register adds nothing more, so the vendor's charge is the only extra cost to budget for.

If your deed also calls for county tax certification, the office recommends ePN because a document router links the two. A single electronic package can then serve both offices.

Searching is its own service. Names are indexed by seller and buyer, and scans reach back to the mid 1800s. The public Tapestry link charges for use, and title professionals may take a Laredo subscription arranged by phone.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies to a Benzie County deed?
sections.html:
Michigan's state transfer tax is collected by this office as the deed goes on record, and its page links the county act (MCL 207.505) and the state act (MCL 207.526). The state charge is $3.75 on each $500 of price, a partial block rounding up, or $7.50 per $1,000. Call the office to learn the county amount for your instrument.

Take Benzie's Census median value of $285,700: state tax alone comes to $2,145, because the price spans 572 blocks of $500 after rounding up. That amount deserves a line in any shoreline seller's net sheet.

Some transfers escape the state tax, and the instrument has to say which exemption it claims.

  • A price below $100, loan security papers, leases and mineral interests.
  • A deed passing from a person to a son, daughter, stepchild or grandchild.
  • A court order that sets no dollar price, a boundary adjustment, or a corrective quitclaim.
  • A land contract in which the seller still holds title, and foreclosure deeds, including deeds given to avoid foreclosure.

sections.h2: What kinds of instruments does Benzie County record?
sections.html:
The office lists its services as the recording of land related paper, and the list is broad. A seller or an heir will meet several of these during a sale or estate settlement.

  • Warranty, quit claim and mineral deeds, as well as administrator, tax and sheriff's deeds.
  • Mortgages, along with assignments and discharges of them.
  • Liens for state and federal tax, circuit court orders, and probate orders.
  • Certificates of trust, master deeds, rights of way, restrictions and subdivision plats.
  • Surveys, land corner records and remonumentation records.

Payoff paperwork matters most with an older loan. A lender files a discharge once a mortgage is satisfied, and the buyer's closer checks this index for it before title is cleared.

sections.h2: What should a Benzie County seller do before filing a deed?
sections.html:
Sequence matters at a small counter. Begin with the title commitment, so you know which liens need a discharge. If the deed has a warranty clause, request the Treasurer's certificate next, or send the deed through ePN so certification travels with it. After that, check that the deed states the complete price, because transfer tax follows the stated price.

Last, choose how it gets there. Carry it in on a weekday, post it with a return envelope, or let the closing agent send it through one of the four vendors. A family transfer should name its exemption right on the instrument, so the tax is not collected in error.

sections.h2: Which neighbors of the Register of Deeds should a seller call?
sections.html:
Upstairs in that building is the Treasurer, at 231-882-0011, on the same weekday schedule. The office administers delinquent tax under Public Act 206 and keeps the tax rolls. Online payments of delinquent tax cost 2.49 percent by card (minimum $1.50) or $1.00 by e-check.

Downstairs, Equalization works from Suite 130 at 231-882-0015. It supplies parcel maps, descriptions, values, sales data, tax maps and millage rates, and its page also links a parcel search and FEMA map change forms, handy for lakefront owners.

The Register's page also carries identity crime guidance. A free Property Fraud Alert service emails you when any document is recorded under your name, which helps an owner who lives elsewhere catch a forged deed early. The office keeps related handouts on preventing identity theft, and the Register collects the state remonumentation fee as part of each filing.

Separately, the Register leads the county Plat Board that reviews new subdivisions and processes U.S. passport applications.

sections.h2: How do Benzie County housing numbers look?
sections.html:
Benzie is small and growing. Census puts it at 18,568 people in 2025, up 3.3 percent from the 2020 base, on 319.7 square miles of land. Nearly a third of residents, 31.1 percent, are 65 or older.

The county counts 12,682 housing units against only 7,708 households, and 87.8 percent of occupied homes belong to their occupants. The 2020 to 2024 median value is $285,700, with household income near $74,834 a year. Builders pulled 136 permits in 2025. Median gross rent is $1,026 a month, a useful benchmark if the house you are selling has a tenant living in it. Because units outnumber households so widely, ask the title agent early whether any owner or heir lives out of the area, since that changes where papers are signed and mailed.

faqs.q: What is Benzie County's fee for filing a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars a document, no matter how long it is. A paper that assigns or discharges several instruments adds three dollars for each one after the first.

faqs.q: Does the Benzie County Register of Deeds add a surcharge for electronic filing?
faqs.a: No. Only the vendor you pick bills a fee, and the approved list is Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm.

faqs.q: When is a tax certificate required in Benzie County?
faqs.a: Warranty deeds, land contracts and condominium master deeds need one. Up to five descriptions cost $5.00, and each further description is 20 cents.

faqs.q: Will Benzie County staff write my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. Staff do not prepare blank documents or give legal advice, so engage an attorney or a title company.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Benzie County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8:30 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon, in Suite 202 of the Government Center in Beulah. Phone 231-882-0016 first if you have a question.
